places.name: Colmar, France
places.connection: Primary visual inspiration for Sophie's hometown, particularly the 'Petite Venise' quarter with its half-timbered houses and canals.

places.name: Riquewihr, France
places.connection: Another Alsatian village whose well-preserved 16th-century architecture heavily influenced the film's townscapes.

places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where the film was produced. The Ghibli Museum is nearby in Mitaka.

places.name: Vienna Secession Building
places.connection: The architecture of the royal city of Kingsbury shows a strong influence from the Vienna Secession art movement, exemplified by this building.

places.name: Venice Film Festival (Palazzo del Cinema)
places.connection: The film had its world premiere at the 61st Venice International Film Festival in 2004, where it competed for the Golden Lion.

places.name: Isle of Man
places.connection: Author Diana Wynne Jones stated the rugged landscapes of the Isle of Man were an inspiration for her depiction of 'The Waste'.

places.name: Dolby Theatre
places.connection: Venue for the 78th Academy Awards, where 'Howl's Moving Castle' was nominated for Best Animated Feature.

places.name: Walt Disney Studios
places.connection: Headquarters of the company that produced and distributed the English-language dub of the film, overseen by Pixar's Pete Docter.

places.name: Kazakh Steppe, Kazakhstan
places.connection: The film's vast, rolling green landscapes of 'The Waste' were visually inspired by the scenery of the Kazakh Steppe.

places.name: Toho Studios
places.connection: The primary Japanese film studio that served as the domestic theatrical distributor for 'Howl's Moving Castle'.
